newsitem.title: USA: Clinton picks Labor Department offical for OPIC.
newsitem.headline: Clinton picks Labor Department offical for OPIC.

text.p: President Clinton has decided to appoint Bernard Anderson, a Labour Department official, to the board of directors of the Overseas Private Investment Corp., the White House said Wednesday.

Anderson, currently the assistant secretary for the Employment Standards Administration at the Labour Department, had run his own economic and management advisory firm in Philadelphia before joining the administration.
OPIC insures U.S. companies' investments abroad from risks including takeover of their assets by foreign governments. OPIC has a 15-member board that sets its underwriting and lending policies.
The White House made the announcement in Michigan, where Clinton was campaigning for next week's election.
